requirement: Proxy an upstream forecast API from aiohttp.web through one ClientSession created at startup and closed at cleanup, mapping upstream 404s, other errors and connection failures to 404 and 502 responses.
skeleton: Typed AppKeys for the upstream URL and session, a cleanup_ctx generator owning the session, a weather handler mapping upstream results and connection errors to HTTP exceptions, and make_app.
caption: A proxy endpoint in aiohttp.web that shares one upstream ClientSession. UPSTREAM_KEY and SESSION_KEY are typed web.AppKey entries. client_session_ctx is registered in app.cleanup_ctx: it opens aiohttp.ClientSession with base_url set to the upstream, stores it under SESSION_KEY, yields while the app serves, and awaits session.close on cleanup. weather(request) reads the city from match_info and calls session.get on /forecast with a city query param. An upstream 404 raises web.HTTPNotFound saying unknown city, any other non-200 status raises web.HTTPBadGateway saying upstream error, and aiohttp.ClientConnectionError becomes HTTPBadGateway saying upstream unavailable. Success returns JSON with the city and temp_c. The fixture asserts, with an upstream and a proxy TestServer, that oslo proxies 3.5 with the city param, that three requests reuse one upstream connection and the session is open while serving and closed after shutdown, that atlantis is 404, that an upstream 429 is 502 upstream error, and that a refused upstream port is 502 upstream unavailable.

plan.intent: Call a downstream API from web handlers without leaking connections
constraints: One ClientSession is created in cleanup_ctx and reused by every request
The session is closed when the app cleans up
Other non-200 upstream statuses raise HTTPBadGateway

rationale.teaches: Own long-lived client resources with app.cleanup_ctx, reuse the session for keep-alive, and translate upstream failures into precise HTTP errors.
rationale.why: A session per request defeats connection pooling, a session never closed leaks sockets, and uncaught upstream errors surface as opaque 500s.

ops.docstring: Share one upstream ClientSession across aiohttp.web handlers.

ops.source:
async def client_session_ctx(app: web.Application) -> AsyncIterator[None]:
    """Open the shared upstream session on startup and close it on cleanup."""
    session = aiohttp.ClientSession(base_url=app[UPSTREAM_KEY])
    app[SESSION_KEY] = session
    yield
    await session.close()

def make_app(upstream_url: str) -> web.Application:
    """Build the proxy application for ``upstream_url``."""
    app = web.Application()
    app[UPSTREAM_KEY] = upstream_url
    app.cleanup_ctx.append(client_session_ctx)
    app.router.add_get("/weather/{city}", weather)
    return app

candidates.why_wrong: Each request opens its own ClientSession, so no upstream connection is reused.
The shared session is never closed when the app shuts down.
Unknown cities are reported as 502 upstream errors instead of 404.
A dead upstream escapes as an unhandled 500 instead of 502.
4xx statuses like 429 are parsed as forecasts and crash on the missing field.
